rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes varying both annealing temperature and hold time to control Al diffusion, whereas the paper used fixed short annealing times (30 min to 1 h) at three temperatures (1100–1300 °C) and water quenching to study temperature-dependent phase stability and cooling-induced transformations. Both involve thermal treatments and quenching, but the hypothesis introduces a time variable not used in the paper.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis suggests isothermal annealing at sub-critical temperatures with varied hold times and rapid quenching, while the paper used annealing at 1100–1300 °C under argon for fixed short times (30 min or 1 h) followed by water quenching. The broad regime of high-temperature annealing and quenching is shared, but the specific temperature range and time-control approach differ.
